title: Advanced Graphs: Strongly Connected Components
contract: Count strongly connected components in a directed graph. A singleton is a component even without a self-loop.
brute: boolean[][] reach=new boolean[n][n];for(int i=0;i<n;i++)reach[i][i]=true;for(int[] e:edges)reach[e[0]][e[1]]=true;for(int k=0;k<n;k++){for(int i=0;i<n;i++)for(int j=0;j<n;j++)reach[i][j]|=reach[i][k]&&reach[k][j];emit("Extend directed transitive closure","via",k);}boolean[] used=new boolean[n];int count=0;for(int i=0;i<n;i++)if(!used[i]){count++;for(int j=0;j<n;j++)if(reach[i][j]&&reach[j][i])used[j]=true;}return count;
optimal: List<List<Integer>> g=new ArrayList<>(),reverse=new ArrayList<>();for(int i=0;i<n;i++){g.add(new ArrayList<>());reverse.add(new ArrayList<>());}for(int[] e:edges){g.get(e[0]).add(e[1]);reverse.get(e[1]).add(e[0]);}boolean[] seen=new boolean[n];List<Integer> order=new ArrayList<>();for(int i=0;i<n;i++)if(!seen[i])finish(i,g,seen,order);Arrays.fill(seen,false);int count=0;for(int i=order.size()-1;i>=0;i--){int start=order.get(i);if(seen[start])continue;count++;Deque<Integer> q=new ArrayDeque<>();q.push(start);seen[start]=true;while(!q.isEmpty()){int u=q.pop();for(int v:reverse.get(u))if(!seen[v]){seen[v]=true;q.push(v);}}emit("Explore one component on reversed edges","start",start,"components",count,"visited",seen);}return count;
reasoning: Mutual reachability defines an SCC, but computing it for all vertex pairs is expensive.
Kosaraju first records vertices by DFS finishing time, then explores the reversed graph in reverse finishing order.
This order prevents a second-pass traversal from escaping into an unprocessed component. Recursion in the first pass needs O(V) stack space and may need an explicit stack for very deep graphs.
